title: SO-F-02.2 Canonical project schema, version 1, with authority and merge classes: every entity type declares its owner authority, scope version and merge class, and two incompatible approvals derive to a semantic conflict, never to an applied state
request: Version 2 of this spec, which supersedes SO-F-02 (signed as contract k-so-f-02-canonical-projec-38d008; the SO-F-02 spec file is unchanged and stays on record, and the manifest and RECONCILIATION mark it superseded by this spec). Decided under owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026. Changes from SO-F-02: T1 is kept as it is, with every requirement, criterion and scope entry, and a task T2 is added. The pull request that builds T1 is #354: its design text (docs/PROJECTS.md, the semantic conflict rule) says that the conflict is surfaced and not enforced, because the coordinator reads snapshot() and nothing in src/ calls view('task') or conflicts(), so a task with an unresolved approve and reject can still be claimed. T2 closes that gap: the read side of the coordinator in src/engine/coordinator.mjs (claim, the eligibility check, status and the task listing around _tasksOf) reads store.view('task') and refuses to claim a task that the view shows as CONFLICTED; its writes keep using snapshot(), so a conflicted task is never written back as CONFLICTED. T2 starts once #354 merges, because view('task') and conflicts() exist only there. Build layer of the Scope One programme, adapted from the fold of 30 Oct 2026 (fold id SO-F-02) and validated against memev main at d1c65ef. Contracts marked with a dagger are signed in the owner's vault and are not visible in this repository; they are cited by id only. Implements the design records SO-1.07 (Relationship model: explicit relations between project items, and change propagation that marks affected work stale); SO-2.01 (Organisational knowledge model: relationships between people, teams, projects, decisions, artefacts and evidence) (contracts/scope-one/specs). The decision record cites this contract by id and keeps only the gaps this one does not cover. Builds on signed vault contracts: SO-04-A†, SO-07-A†, WO-05-A†. Memev contracts that land first: SO-F-01, SO-1.01. Source in the fold: #222 section 13.7 (convergence of state is not proof of truth; the event, receipt and evidence model) and #223 ARCHITECTURAL-INTERDEPENDENCIES.md (structured state convergence requires canonical schemas, ownership and conflict policy). Settled decisions this contract follows (owner decision 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md): topology is local-first and the cloud is only a relay and a backup; every supported provider stands on equal footing and no work or tier depends on one; crdt-merge is reached only through the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs (docs/EXTENSION-POINTS.md) and this contract adds no merge engine to the core; tiers follow docs/PRICING.md (Free core, Personal for up to 3 computers with no per-computer add-on, higher tiers by contacting us) with no Personal trial; the git backup keeps running every few minutes (sync.interval_min). Memory authority: ADR 7 (memory and project-state authority) is proposed in PR #325 and is not decided here; this contract cites it and the local-first decision, and keeps one store under the vault with no second database. Provenance: adapted from the fold of 30 Oct 2026. Changes: (1) converted from the vault task format to the memev spec format (named tests run as red-green checks on the own test file of the contract; inline regular expression flags became the flags key; hygiene and decision verifiers became commands or doc checks). (2) removed fold-only fields and the owner-decision marker field, reworded the stop rule that named a patent, and made the text pass the leak scan. (3) Prerequisite SO-1.01 added: the state machine and store are now wired, so the semantic-conflict rule acts on the real transition table. (4) Boundary with PG-05.1 WP05-01 (merge-semantics table by object class, docs/MERGE-SEMANTICS.md): the vocabulary of semantics is owned there. This contract owns the declaration on every entity type, the store refusing an entity without one, and the semantic-conflict rule. The four class names in the schema must equal the semantics column of that table; neither contract redefines the other.

tasks.description: The convergence engine merges one note against a base today. Before it can touch projects, tasks, decisions or evidence, every entity type needs a declared merge class (last-writer, set union, append-only, human resolution) and an authority owner. The re-derivation of state from events is SO-07-A AC03 and the version conflict is SO-04-A AC06; this contract adds the schema and the semantic part those do not catch. The core applies no merge class itself: the free path keeps both versions and the engine contract is SO-F-06 (the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs, ADR 6).

tasks.title: The coordinator reads the conflict: claim, eligibility and status read store.view('task'), and a task with unresolved approve and reject approvals cannot be claimed
requirements: the read side of the coordinator in src/engine/coordinator.mjs (claim, the eligibility check, status and the task listing around _tasksOf) reads store.view('task'), so a task that the view shows as CONFLICTED is not eligible and cannot be claimed (source: docs/PROJECTS.md, the semantic conflict rule of pull request #354, the wiring that follows)

the writes of the coordinator keep using snapshot(), so a conflicted task is never written back as CONFLICTED and the stored status stays the one the task had (source: docs/PROJECTS.md, the semantic conflict rule of pull request #354)
no change to the store, the schema or the conflict derivation: those are T1 and pull request #354; this task only consumes them (source: owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026)
tasks.description: Repo: memev. Starts once pull request #354 (T1) merges: store.view('task') and store.conflicts() exist only there. A task with unresolved approve and reject approvals shows as CONFLICTED in the view while its stored status is unchanged. Today the coordinator reads snapshot() everywhere, so such a task can be claimed. This task changes only the read side (claim, the eligibility check, status and the listing around _tasksOf) to read the view; every write still reads and writes through snapshot(). The coordinator unit tests run over a store double: the double gains a view method that returns the snapshot, so they stay as they are. SO-A-01, SO-A-03 and PGP-1.02 also list src/engine/coordinator.mjs in their scope: land this change after those that are open, or merge main into this branch first.

criteria.statement: a task with unresolved approve and reject approvals (CONFLICTED in store.view('task'), stored status unchanged) cannot be claimed: claim refuses it, eligible does not list it and status reports it as conflicted; the test builds the two approvals on a real store, fails on the current code, where claim succeeds, and passes after the change
